issues.legal_issue: Requisitioning premises to provide living accommodation for an employee of a public utility corporation may serve a public purpose when the accommodation is a statutory activity essential to the efficient performance of the corporation’s public services.
material_facts: The government requisitioned premises to house an officer of a road transport corporation that was a public utility concern.
The requisition did not name a particular individual, and the premises were available to the corporation to house an officer to be named later.
The officer was required to perform duties in the relevant city, and the corporation appointed officers it considered necessary for the efficient performance of its functions.
The corporation had statutory power to provide living accommodation for employees.

The court found that accommodation for the corporation’s employees was essential to the efficient operation of the road transport system, with which the community’s general interest was directly and vitally concerned.
issues.conclusion: The requisition was for a public purpose and was validly made.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 5(1) of the Bombay Land Requisition Act, 1948, requisition must be for a public purpose. Sections 14, 18, 19(1)(c), and 19(2)(a) and (b) of the Road Transport Corporations Act, 1950, read together, establish the corporation’s functions and its power to provide employee accommodation as part of its statutory activities. A purpose is public when the community’s general interest, rather than merely an individual’s particular interest, is directly and vitally concerned. Applying Hamabai Framjee Petit v. Secretary of State for India in Council, State of Bombay v. Bhanji Munji, and State of Bombay v. Ali Gulshan, the Court held that accommodation essential to the efficient functioning of a public utility corporation can serve that public interest.

rule.if: land_requisition_for_employee_housing and public_utility_employer and statutory_employee_housing_function and employee_needed_for_efficient_service and accommodation_essential_to_public_service

predicates.land_requisition_for_employee_housing: The proceeding concerns land requisitioned to provide living accommodation for an employee.
predicates.public_utility_employer: The employee’s employer provides a public utility service whose activities directly and vitally concern the community’s general interest.
predicates.statutory_employee_housing_function: The employer has statutory authority to provide living accommodation for its employees as part of its activities.
predicates.employee_needed_for_efficient_service: The employer requires the employee to perform duties necessary for the efficient performance of its functions.
predicates.accommodation_essential_to_public_servic: Providing accommodation for employees is essential to the efficient operation of the public service.

issues.definition: When premises are requisitioned for an employee of a public utility employer, and the employer has a statutory housing function, needs the employee for efficient service, and requires accommodation to support that service, the requisition serves a public purpose.

issues.legal_issue: Whether a requisition serves a public purpose must be assessed from the circumstances of the particular case, and courts have a duty to decide that issue when it is raised.
material_facts: The validity of the requisition was challenged on the ground that it was not for a public purpose.
The government relied on the public utility character of the corporation and the relationship between employee accommodation and its efficient functioning.
The Court considered the facts and circumstances bearing on whether the community’s general interest was directly and vitally concerned.
issues.conclusion: The expression “public purpose” cannot be precisely defined; the government is prima facie the best judge of whether a requisition serves that purpose, but it is not the sole judge, and courts have jurisdiction and a duty to decide the issue when it is raised.
issues.legal_principle: A public purpose includes an object in which the general interest of the community, as opposed to the particular interest of individuals, is directly and vitally concerned. The meaning cannot be precisely defined in the abstract, and each case requires close examination of its facts and circumstances. The Court relied on Hamabai Framjee Petit v. Secretary of State for India in Council, State of Bombay v. Bhanji Munji, and State of Bombay v. Ali Gulshan.

predicates.public_purpose_challenged_in_requisition: A party challenges a requisition on the ground that it does not serve a public purpose.

issues.definition: When a requisition’s public purpose is challenged, the court must assess whether the community’s general interest is directly and vitally concerned by examining the circumstances of the case.
